ideas.title: Theme Conflict Merge
ideas.summary: For small Shopify merchants whose theme update failed with 'code edits could not be included': upload the old and new theme, get back a merged copy with your edits carried over file by file and a plain-language list of the few places that need a decision.

public.summary: When a theme update refuses to keep your custom changes, this carries them over for you and shows you only the few spots that need a decision.
public.problem: You paid someone to tweak your store's theme, and now the theme has an update with fixes you want. You click update and get a message that your code edits could not be included, so the new version arrives without any of your changes. Your choices are to stay on the old version, hire a developer to copy everything across by hand, or hope you remember what was changed.
public.forWhom: Shop owners on Shopify who have edited their theme, or had someone edit it for them, and want to keep getting theme updates.
benefits: Keep your custom changes when you update your theme
Know exactly which changes need a human decision, in plain words
Stop paying a developer every time the theme updates
See the updated store side by side with the old one before anything goes live
Your live store stays untouched until you choose to switch

ideas.problemStatement: I tried to update my theme and Shopify said a copy was added but my code edits could not be included because 'Rebase failed with conflicts' on ten files. I don't know which of my changes are missing, and copying old files over the new version breaks the update itself.
ideas.description: The merchant downloads two theme ZIPs from the Shopify admin (the live, customized theme and the new version Shopify added to the library) and uploads them. The tool finds the stock version the store was originally installed from (public release tags for Horizon and Dawn on GitHub; other themes need the merchant's original ZIP) and runs a three-way merge file by file, so that one conflict no longer throws away every edit, which is what Shopify's built-in updater does today. Non-conflicting customizations are applied automatically; each real conflict is shown as a short plain-language card ('you changed the cart button text here; the update also changed this button') with a choose-mine, choose-theirs, or ask-a-developer option. Store-specific files (settings_data.json, locales, JSON templates) are labeled as settings, not code, so they do not drown the list. The output is a merged ZIP the merchant uploads as an unpublished theme, plus side-by-side screenshots of the home, product and cart pages for a visual check.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners of small Shopify stores (one to ten staff) on Horizon or Dawn who have edited theme code themselves, with Sidekick, or through a past freelancer, and whose theme update reported that code edits could not be included.
ideas.buyer: The store owner, on the business card, from the same budget that pays for apps and occasional freelance theme work (one freelancer.com job for this task offered $30 to $250).
ideas.whyNow: Horizon, Shopify's newest free theme, ships updates every few weeks (3.3.1 to 3.5.1 to 4.14 to 4.15 in 2026), and Shopify's own updater drops all code edits when any file conflicts. Shopify staff said in August 2025 they were working on it, and the thread was still open in September 2026. The paid updater with 291 reviews (OOTS) does not list Horizon among the themes it supports.
ideas.founderFit: Three-way merge is version control, which Pisan teaches, and the core is a deterministic diff3 over text files that he can build and test alone with real theme release tags. It needs no paid API at runtime and no access to the merchant's store in the first version, because it works on downloaded ZIPs.

competitors.gap: Lists Dawn and partner themes but not Horizon; 1 and 2 star reviews say customizations are still lost.

competitors.name: Theme Drift: Compare & Diff
competitors.gap: Shows three-way conflicts but leaves the merge to the merchant or to a paid migration service.

competitors.name: DiffMate
competitors.gap: Diff editor that copies changes between themes one by one; no automatic merge.

competitors.gap: Read-only plain-English report of custom code; Dawn only; does not produce a merged theme.

keyFeatures: Three-way merge per file against the stock release the store started from
Automatic carry-over of non-conflicting edits, so one conflict no longer drops everything
Plain-language conflict cards with mine / theirs / ask-a-developer choices
Settings files labeled as settings, not code
Side-by-side screenshots of home, product and cart pages
A developer hand-off note listing only the unresolved conflicts

features: Upload two theme ZIPs; Horizon and Dawn base versions fetched from public GitHub tags
diff3 merge per file with conflict cards
Merged ZIP download for upload as an unpublished theme
outOfScope: Writing to the store through the Admin API (needs Shopify's protected Asset access scope)
Third-party paid themes without a merchant-supplied original ZIP

ideas.techStack: React + Vite, a browser-side diff3 library (no upload of theme code to a server in the free check), Supabase for accounts and payments, Playwright for screenshots in a later version.

pricing.model: Per update, with a cheap subscription for frequent Horizon updaters
pricing.rationale: Sits between Theme Drift's $19.99 one-time compare and the $30 to $250 a merchant offers a freelancer for the same job; under OOTS's $9/month.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: 150 merchants a month at $19 = $2,850/month, assuming a 2 to 3 percent conversion from free conflict checks driven by forum answers. Unvalidated.
ideas.distribution: Answer the recurring 'code edits could not be included' and 'rebase failed with conflicts' threads on community.shopify.com with a free conflict check; list on the Shopify App Store only after the ZIP version proves demand.

validationTest.method: Ship the free browser-only check (upload two ZIPs, see how many edits would carry over and how many conflict) and offer the merged ZIP for $19 to merchants found in forum threads.
validationTest.successCriteria: Out of 40 free checks, 8 or more paid merges, and at least 5 merchants who report the merged theme went live without a developer.
validationTest.cost: About 2 weeks of evenings and $0 beyond hosting.

ideas.moat: Weak. The merge itself is standard; the defensible part would be a library of per-theme base versions and file-type rules (JSON templates, settings, locales) tuned on real merges. Shopify could fix its updater at any time.
compliance: Shopify app review: writing assets back to a theme from a public app needs Shopify's protected Asset access scope, so the first version works on downloaded ZIPs and never writes to the store.
Privacy: theme code can contain API keys or tracking IDs; the free check runs in the browser and nothing is stored.
Licensing: paid themes' code is licensed to the merchant; the tool must not keep or redistribute base versions of paid themes.

risks.risk: Shopify ships a better merge in its built-in updater (staff said they were working on it).
risks.mitigation: Keep the build small and ZIP-based; pivot the conflict cards into a developer hand-off tool if Shopify closes the gap.

risks.risk: Liquid and JSON merges that are textually clean but break the store.
risks.mitigation: Always output an unpublished theme, show page screenshots, and never publish.

risks.risk: Crowded category: seven theme diff and update apps, four launched in 2026.
risks.mitigation: Compete on the one thing none of them does for Horizon: produce a merged theme, not a diff.

scoreRationale.pain: Four independent merchants in 2026 hit failed or damaging theme updates: https://community.shopify.com/t/update-theme-error-rebase-failed-with-conflicts/630057 and https://community.shopify.com/t/i-have-a-problem-with-my-store/675548
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: One dated paid job ($30 to $250, https://www.freelancer.com/projects/git/Shopify-Theme-Update-Diff-Migrate) and a $9/month app with 291 reviews (https://apps.shopify.com/theme-updater-by-out-of-the-sandbox); reviewer: people pay to have it done, not much for software.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve via forum answers, but the App Store category is crowded with 7+ theme diff/update apps (https://apps.shopify.com/theme-change-monitor).
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Shopify's free updater already merges non-conflicting edits (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/themes/managing-themes/updating-themes); Theme Drift sells a 3-way compare for $19.99.
scoreRationale.feasibility: A correct merge across Liquid, JSON templates, settings and locales is harder than it looks, as the Theme Drift feedback thread notes: https://community.shopify.com/t/looking-for-merchants-agencies-who-struggle-when-a-customized-theme-gets-an-update-feedback-on-theme-drift-2-3-way-theme-compare/686301
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: Writing a merged theme from a public app needs Shopify's protected Asset access scope (https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest/latest/resources/asset), which is why the first version works on ZIPs.

review.findings: Adversarial reviewer recommended a kill and rescored from 23 to 17: competitiveGap 2->1 because Shopify's free updater already carries over non-conflicting edits and Theme Drift ($19.99 one-time 3-way compare), DiffMate (free) and Theme Upgrade Buddy (free) cover the compare-and-copy step; WTP 4->3 because the paid evidence is one $30-250 freelancer job and a $9/month app; reachability 4->3 (7+ apps in the category); feasibility 4->3 (Liquid/JSON/settings merge is hard); compliance 5->3 (theme asset writes need a protected scope). The reviewer also identified the one remaining wedge: Shopify's updater is all or nothing, so a single conflict drops every edit, and OOTS does not list Horizon. The idea was re-scoped to exactly that case, working on downloaded ZIPs to avoid the protected scope, and ships as provisional at the reviewer's 17 because it is the only candidate today that survived review with a residual gap; the other five reviewed candidates were killed outright.

missing: competitiveGap 1: Shopify's free updater and several cheap diff apps cover most of the job
gateGap.closedBy: The validation test's paid merges close the largest gap: 8 paid $19 merges out of 40 free checks would show that merchants pay for a merged theme rather than a diff, which would justify raising competitiveGap to 2 and willingnessToPay to 4. Reaching 22 also needs reachability 4, shown by forum answers converting without App Store listing.

watchlist.title: Cross-course content maintenance for Canvas design teams (bulk find, preview, replace and rollback for vendor-driven breakage)
watchlist.targetCustomer: Instructional designers and LMS admin teams who maintain content across dozens to thousands of Canvas courses.
watchlist.problemStatement: Vendor-side changes keep breaking content across many courses at once: Canvas's silent 2026-10-07 change to enhanceable_content tabs, Community guide links moving from /t5/ to /en/kb/, and LTI 1.3 migrations that leave embedded assignment links saying 'deleted'. Teams fix pages one at a time or with shared Tampermonkey scripts.
watchlist.missedGate: competitiveGap 2: Atomic Search already sells account-wide Find & Replace for Canvas, and free community userscripts cover bulk search and link conversion; total below 22. 2026-11-04: re-researched with two freelancer.com searches each (B11); no paid job for the task was found (the Canvas hits were homepage redesigns), so the score is unchanged.

watchlist.title: ADA demand-letter remediation ledger for small Shopify and WordPress stores
watchlist.targetCustomer: Small online store owners who have received an ADA website demand letter or lawsuit
watchlist.problemStatement: Owners who are served do not know where to start, get pitched overlays, and have no dated record of good-faith fixes mapped to the allegations.
watchlist.missedGate: No complaint dated within 180 days (the served owners posted in 2023 to 2025); competitiveGap 2 against remediation vendors and free axe/WAVE. 2026-11-03 extra run: a store owner's 2026-05-12 Shopify Forms review says they were sued over a popup (within 180 days), but Remedy (free plan, launched 2026-08-21) now keeps a dated accessibility record, so competitiveGap stays 2. 2026-11-04: re-researched with two freelancer.com searches each (B11); no paid job for the task was found (the Canvas hits were homepage redesigns), so the score is unchanged.

runNotes.caveats: Only one idea ships, against a first-run target of 3. Six candidates were reviewed and five were killed outright, each because a free or very cheap product already does the job (Flowlert, Lovable's built-in scan, PixelGuard's free plan, free PHP 8.4 scanners); the developer-tooling lens on small-business automation and Shopify surfaced markets crowded with indie tools launched in 2026, and many forum 'complaints' were market-validation posts by those builders. Theme Conflict Merge ships as provisional at 17 although its reviewer recommended a kill: the reviewer's own findings left one gap (Shopify's updater drops every edit when any file conflicts, and the $9/month incumbent does not list Horizon), and the idea was re-scoped to that case. Because one idea ships, the complexity-mix constraint (a Weekend MVP plus a Multi-week) is not met. Watchlist re-research (Canvas maintenance, ADA demand letters, agent exposure audit) found no new payment evidence. A3's GitHub path returned 422 only because queries lacked is:issue; with it the API works. The OOTS evidence date (2025-02-15) is older than 180 days; the freelancer job date comes from the API's time_submitted.
